newsitem.title: USA: Bond issue approved for Milwaukee baseball stadium.
newsitem.headline: Bond issue approved for Milwaukee baseball stadium.

text.p: A government panel charged with building a new ballpark for the Milwaukee Brewers baseball team gave the green light Friday to the sale of $160 million of tax-exempt bonds for the project.
A spokesman for the Southeast Wisconsin Professional Baseball Park District board said the board voted 11 to 2 in favor of the bond resolution.
According to the spokesman, the deal is expected to be priced sometime the week before Christmas.
Next step for the bond issue are meetings next week with rating agencies and bond insurers, Pat Born, a senior vice president at Evenson Dodge Inc., the financial adviser for the deal, has said.
Board members approved the bond issue despite a pending legal challenge to a five-county sales tax slated to repay the bonds.

While a lawsuit, brought by a group of Milwaukee area taxpayers, has been dismissed by the Wisconsin Supreme Court and by a U.S. District Court judge in Milwaukee, the group has filed an appeal of the federal court's dismissal with the U.S. Appellate Court in Chicago.
The group has contended that the 0.1 percent sales tax imposed by the state legislature is unconstitutional.
Analysts at Fitch Investors Service, Moody's Investors Service and Standard & Poor's Corp. said this week they would examine the lawsuit as part of their review of the credit.
Jon Axelrod, an attorney representing state officials in the lawsuit, has said that he would forward an opinion to bond counsel on the $160 million bond issue that the lawsuit has no merit.
Last month, the baseball district board threatened monetary sanctions against the taxpayer litigants if they persist with the lawsuit.
The board spokesman said the board considered a request from the taxpayers to drop the sanctions, but took no action at Friday's meeting.

In addition to proceeds from the bond issue, the $250 million convertible-roofed stadium would be funded with $50 million in loans to the Brewers from the city of Milwaukee, the local business community and two foundations, and $40 million from the sale of naming rights to Miller Brewing Co., upfront concession payments and a $10 million letter of credit from the American Baseball League.
